prerequisites: Basic understanding of physics (mechanics and electricity)
Familiarity with the use of computer tools for technical simulation

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental concepts of automatic control systems and their classification.
Identify and describe the main components of a control system in mechatronic engineering (sensor, actuator, plant, controller).
Know the modeling of physical systems using differential equations, transfer functions, and state-space representations.
Analyze the dynamic behavior of linear systems, both in the time and frequency domains.
Evaluate the stability and performance of control systems using analytical and graphical criteria.
Design and tune classic controllers (especially PID) based on system requirements.
Use simulation tools to validate models and controllers.
Know the basic elements of industrial automation systems, including PLCs, sensors, and actuators.
Apply acquired knowledge in the design and implementation of control solutions for real or simulated mechatronic systems.
Promote the capacity for analysis, problem-solving, and teamwork in the context of control engineering.
Design and develop algorithms on control systems applied to mechatronic engineering.
Know electronic sensor and actuator systems, as well as their implementation and connectivity in mechatronic systems.

Skillfully apply the most relevant computer tools in the development of a mechatronic engineering project such as Matlab, Simulink, OpenModelica, LabView, among others, and use AI for their optimization.
Design, program, and implement centralized and distributed industrial automation systems. (DCS, SCADA, HMI, PLC).
Implement programming in a mechatronic system using languages such as Matlab or Python. Matlab, Python, C++, or Java, among others.
Use specialized bibliography to autonomously update knowledge on materials, manufacturing technologies, and design and applications within mechatronic engineering.
Apply software tools in the design and simulation of a mechatronic system, and its optimization using AI.
Apply AI techniques for optimized control, automation, electronics, and informatics in the design of systems and products in mechatronic engineering.

syllabus_topics: Modeling of Dynamic Systems. Temporal Analysis and Stability.

assessment_methods.method: Lab practice reports and computer lab assignments

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated based on lab practice reports and computer lab assignments (50%) and a practical exam (50%). A minimum score of 5 on the theoretical exam is required to pass the course. To average the scores, a minimum of 3.5 must be obtained in each component. Resit arrangements involve individualized reinforcement for the parts needing improvement.
